page: Amazon Web Services r9g.2xlarge is a memory-optimized compute instance built within the AWS Nitro System framework. It utilizes custom 64-bit Arm architecture AWS Graviton processors operating at a clock speed of 3.3 GHz. The configuration allocates 8 dedicated vCPUs mapped directly to 8 physical execution cores with one thread per core, eliminating virtual resource contention associated with simultaneous multithreading. System memory totals 64 GB, establishing an allocation profile of 8.0 GB of RAM per vCPU.

Hardware specifications for the r9g.2xlarge exclude local block storage and GPU accelerators, which requires external network-attached volumes for all file system storage and persistent state. Host networking is supported with a baseline throughput of 4 Gbps. Infrastructure designs must account for the lack of onboard NVMe disks, and software environments must be compiled for the arm64 instruction set rather than legacy x86 architectures.

Qualitatively, the Arm-based architecture combined with an 8:1 memory-to-vCPU ratio delivers high memory density per compute unit. This profile offers resource efficiency for systems bound primarily by active memory footprint rather than heavy floating-point calculation. The r9g.2xlarge is suited for in-memory databases, distributed memory caches, relational database management systems, and memory-intensive data processing pipelines.
description: Amazon Web Services r9g.2xlarge is a memory-optimized cloud server built on the AWS Nitro hypervisor architecture. Powered by 64-bit Arm-based AWS Graviton processors, the instance delivers 8 physical cores operating at 3.3 GHz without simultaneous multithreading, providing 8 dedicated vCPUs. It is configured with 64 GB of system memory, maintaining an allocation ratio of 8.0 GB per vCPU to accommodate memory-intensive operations. The instance does not feature local storage disks or integrated GPU hardware accelerators, necessitating external network-attached volumes for data persistence. Network traffic is supported by a 4 Gbps baseline bandwidth capacity. Due to its custom Arm architecture and high memory-to-core ratio, r9g.2xlarge offers favorable resource density and operating efficiency for applications requiring substantial working memory. The instance is suited for in-memory caches, relational database systems, memory-bound data analysis pipelines, enterprise application hosting, and distributed memory store deployments.
